title: consumption populism: how business leaders use populist logic to shape consumption
core_idea: Introduce and conceptualize 'consumption populism' as a non-essentialist, discursive process through which business leaders construct 'the people' to shape consumption. The study applies Laclau's populism and a discursive-hegemonic model to a case (Baba Ramdev's neo-swadeshi practices) and develops a three-stage process model—otherization, homogenization, hegemony— enacted via practices of mobilizing affect, creating spectacles, and posing impossible demands, while interrogating the role of affect, ethical implications for vulnerable consumers, neoliberal elites, and the possibility of a non-exclusionary agonistic form.
tldr: This article proposes 'consumption populism' and a three-stage model of how business leaders use populist logic and affective practices to construct collective consumer identities and shape consumption, illustrated with a case study and discussion of ethical and political implications.
